text:
Marathon Petroleum jumped 3.9% today to $476.87, extending a remarkable two-week rally of over 21%. The stock's surge reflects tightening global oil supply conditions: Brent crude topped $106 after a deadly attack on a Saudi airport, while geopolitical tensions—including a potential U.S. strike on Iranian nuclear sites and ongoing Houthi attacks in the Middle East—are creating concerns about disruptions to oil shipments. U.S. refineries are running at 92.7% capacity, and with global oil prices well above domestic prices ($125 versus $96 per barrel), refiners like Marathon profit from the ability to process cheap domestic crude and sell refined products into a higher-priced global market.

The broader context here is that crude oil supply fears are outweighing the modest boost from Trump's reported diesel deal with Russia—a deal that analysts note would cover less than two weeks of U.S. demand anyway. Rising geopolitical risk in the Middle East, combined with tight refinery operations and wide price gaps between U.S. and global oil markets, creates the kind of environment where independent refiners typically see margin expansion and stronger profitability.
